title: Inference gateway 5xx surge: root-cause, targeted hotfix, and customer-guided retry shim
creator: Alexandra Kim
description: Several customers reported multi-tenant visible failures characterized by synchronous 5xx responses from the inference gateway during high-tail request bursts. Impact manifests as client-side timeouts and aggressive SDK retries that amplify pressure. This ticket captures the investigation, root cause analysis, immediate hotfix, and a medium-term resilient fallback (async queue + client-guided retry shim).
steps_to_reproduce: Run a burst workload with 100 concurrent streaming generation requests across 10 tenants with varied seq-lens
Simulate SDK clients using default retry policy: 3 retries with exponential backoff starting at 250ms
Observe gateway returning 502/504 for ~6-12% of requests during sustained 30s bursts and subsequent retry amplification causing queueing at edge proxies
impact_summary: High error rates and visible timeouts for multiple paying customers during peak inference bursts; supporting tickets opened with CS; SLO breaches for p95 latency and p99 error budget nearing exhaustion in affected regions.
observed_metrics_and_traces: edge_gateway_5xx_rate > baseline by 14% during burst windows
connection_pool_saturation_time increases correlated with KV cache eviction spikes
trace snippets show requests spending >200ms in frontdoor queue before gateway circuit short-circuits with 502
downstream runtime logs show temporary kernel scheduling stalls when sequence-length variance high
root_cause: A confluence of factors: (1) edge inference gateway began rejecting requests under queue shear due to an aggressive per-connection hard limit introduced in a prior optimization; (2) high variance in sequence lengths caused runtime kernel selection jitter that temporarily delayed token generation startup for some streams; (3) client SDK retries with short backoff repeatedly re-entered the gateway, amplifying the saturation effect (retry storm). The net effect was transient queue exhaust and circuit-triggered 5xx responses rather than graceful async enqueueing.
mitigation_actions_taken: Rolled back the per-connection hard limit at the gateway to previous soft-queue behavior (hotfix v1.23.1) — immediate reduction in 5xx observed
Applied short-term increase in connection pool and accept queue sizes in affected front-door hosts
Disabled a recently-added 'fast-fail long-tail' heuristic that misclassified slow-start streams as hung
Customer comms: published incident summary to affected customers and provided suggested SDK backoff patch to reduce immediate retry amplification
proposed_long_term_fix: Introduce an async fallback queue for requests that hit gateway admission limits: requests accepted and queued on durable fast-path with tokenized client receipt for polling or streaming fallback
Implement 'guided-retry' headers in our SDKs and REST clients so retries use server-recommended backoff windows to avoid stampeding (server sends Retry-After hints derived from current queue depth)
Enhance kernel-selection telemetry and add a pre-flight fast-path to stabilize slow-start for variable sequence lengths
Add per-tenant adaptive admission control that uses recent tail-latency signals rather than hard connection counts
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (hotfix): rollback hard-limit and queue size bump — deployed to us-west-2 and eu-west-1 on 2026-03-11 (complete)
Stage 2 (sdk guidance): ship SDK patch with conservative default backoff and support for Retry-After hints — target 2026-03-18
Stage 3 (async fallback): design + API spec + feature flag rollout in runtime-1.23.2 — canary to 5% traffic 2026-04-01, full rollout 2026-04-15
Stage 4 (adaptive admission): telemetry-driven rollout with per-tenant thresholds behind a console toggle — Q2 milestone
monitoring_queries: alert if edge_gateway_5xx_rate > 0.01 for 10m AND queue_depth > 50
communication_and_documents: Incident channel: #inc-389217 (meeting notes and triage logs)
Customer-facing note: emailed affected accounts with temporary mitigations and ETA for SDK patch
decision_log: Do not throttle client retries at edge proxy level — will break client semantics for private deployments; instead, prefer server-guided retry hints
Async fallback chosen over immediate request drop to preserve availability for bursty workloads and provide deterministic client experience
Roll back hard-limit as immediate corrective because it caused more tail failures than it saved in load-shedding

Merge SDK backoff PR and publish patch release notes — owner @Priya Reddy
Implement pre-flight kernel telemetry probe in runtime to detect slow-start patterns — owner @Anwar Haddad

SDK adoption: >75% of active client instances upgraded to new backoff within 30 days for customers on managed SDKs
Async fallback canary remains stable for 7 days at 5% traffic before expanding
